question: Why is even immense material wealth insufficient compared to this kaula teaching?
premises: One might possess vast accumulated wealth
That wealth could fill an ocean with jewels
Such wealth is set up as a comparison
inference: Even wealth vast enough to fill the ocean with jewels is incomparable to this teaching.
uncertainties: ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is a fused and irregular form; parsing is tentative
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to make the ocean filled with jewels.
